'''Russell Scott Lande''' {{post-nominals|country=GBR|FRS}} (born 1951) is an American [[evolutionary biologist]] and [[ecologist]], and an International Chair Professor at [[Centre for Biodiversity Dynamics]] at the [[Norwegian University of Science and Technology]] (NTNU). He is a [[fellow of the Royal Society]] and a member of the [[United States National Academy of Sciences]].<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.nasonline.org/news-and-multimedia/news/april-28-2015-NAS-Election.html |title=April 28, 2015: NAS Members and Foreign Associates Elected |accessdate=2015-05-08 |url-status=dead |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20151120211335/http://www.nasonline.org/news-and-multimedia/news/april-28-2015-NAS-Election.html |archivedate=2015-11-20 }}</ref>

==Education and career==

He received his Ph.D. in 1976 from [[Harvard University]] where he was a student of [[Richard Lewontin]], and completed his Postdoctoral work at the [[University of Wisconsin]] under [[James F. Crow]]. He then held positions at the [[University of Chicago]], [[University of Oregon]], [[University of California, San Diego]],<ref name="ucsd">{{Cite web|url=https://biology.ucsd.edu/research/faculty/rlande|title=Russell Lande}}</ref> and [[Imperial College London]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.imperial.ac.uk/people/r.lande|title = Home - Emeritus Professor Russell Lande}}</ref>

In 2016, he was employed as an International Chair Professor at the [[Norwegian University of Science and Technology]] (NTNU).<ref>[http://www.ntnu.edu/cbd/people employees at CBD,  NTNU]</ref>

==Work==

Lande is best known for his early work extending [[quantitative genetics]] theory to the context of [[evolutionary biology]] in natural populations. In particular, he developed a [[stochastic]] theory for the evolution of quantitative traits by [[genetic drift]] and [[natural selection]].<ref name="ucsd" /> He also proposed a multivariate framework to describe the effect of selection on multiple correlated characters, thus helping clarify the much-debated notion of genetic constraints in phenotypic evolution.<ref name="balzan" /> He later applied and extended these results to study a wide variety of topics in evolutionary biology, including: [[sexual selection]], [[speciation]], the evolution of [[phenotypic plasticity]], of [[self-fertilization]], of [[life history theory|life history]], of a [[species range]] in space and time.<ref>Lande, Russel «Sexual Dimorphism, Sexual Selection, and Adaptation in Polygenic Characters». In: ''Evolution'', vol. 34, no. 2 (Mar. 1980), pp. 292–305</ref>

Apart from his work in evolutionary genetics, Lande has substantially contributed to the fields of [[population dynamics]]  and [[conservation biology]].<ref name="balzan">{{Cite web|url=http://www.balzan.org/en/prizewinners/russell-scott-lande|title=Fondazione Balzan}}</ref> In particular, his model on the effect of [[habitat fragmentation]] on the [[extinction threshold]] of territorial species was central to the debate about the conservation of the [[Northern spotted owl]] in the Pacific Northwest.<ref>Fisch (2012)</ref> He and [[Georgina Mace]] contributed to clarify the categories for the [[IUCN red list]], by proposing new criteria based on measurable quantities relating to times to [[extinction]].<ref name="balzan" /> He is a specialist of [[stochastic]] population dynamics, on which he co-authored a book with [[Steinar Engen]] and [[Bernt-Erik Sæther]], and of methods for estimating [[density dependence]] from [[time series]] of population density.

Some of the concepts and tools he introduced, such as the phenotypic [[selection gradient]] (univariate or multivariate, directional or quadratic) and the '''G''' matrix, have become standard in evolutionary biology.<ref name="balzan" />

* [[Balzan Prize]] 2011<ref name="balzan" />

* Elected member, [[United States National Academy of Sciences]] 2015<ref>[https://www.nasonline.org/directory-entry/russell-s-lande-dkqnvu/ NAS on the election]</ref>
* Outstanding Paper Award, [[The Wildlife Society]] (TWS) 2015<ref>[http://wildlife.org/wildlife-publication-awards/ TWS on the award]</ref>
